sql: SELECT t.id, t2.label FROM s.t INNER JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id

sql: SELECT t2.id, t2.t_id FROM s.t2 LEFT JOIN s.t ON t2.t_id = t.id

sql: SELECT t2.id, t2.t_id FROM s.t2 LEFT OUTER JOIN s.t ON t2.t_id = t.id

sql: SELECT t.id, t2.label FROM s.t RIGHT JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id

sql: SELECT t.id, t2.label FROM s.t RIGHT OUTER JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id

sql: SELECT t.id, t2.label FROM s.t FULL JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id
note: FULL JOIN with ON clause

sql: SELECT t.id, t2.label FROM s.t FULL OUTER JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id
note: FULL OUTER JOIN with ON clause

sql: SELECT * FROM s.t CROSS JOIN s.t2
note: CROSS JOIN (no ON/USING)

sql: SELECT t.id, t2.t_id FROM s.t JOIN s.t2 USING (id)
note: JOIN USING with shared column name

sql: SELECT a.id, b.id FROM s.t AS a JOIN s.t AS b ON a.id <> b.id
note: self join with aliases

sql: SELECT t.id, sub.label FROM s.t JOIN (SELECT t_id, label FROM s.t2) AS sub ON t.id = sub.t_id

sql: SELECT t.id, t2.label, p.kind FROM s.t JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id JOIN s.parent AS p ON t.id = p.id

sql: SELECT t.id, lf.* FROM s.t, LATERAL (SELECT * FROM s.t2 WHERE t2.t_id = t.id) AS lf
note: LATERAL subquery in FROM comma list

sql: SELECT t.id, lf.* FROM s.t JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM s.t2 WHERE t2.t_id = t.id) AS lf ON true
note: JOIN LATERAL subquery with ON true

sql: SELECT t.id FROM (s.t JOIN s.t2 ON s.t.id = s.t2.t_id)
note: parenthesized join expression in FROM

sql: SELECT * FROM s.t NATURAL JOIN s.t2
note: NATURAL JOIN (auto-matches common columns)

sql: SELECT * FROM s.t2 NATURAL LEFT JOIN s.t
note: NATURAL LEFT JOIN

sql: SELECT t.id, rf.* FROM s.t LEFT JOIN LATERAL s.rows_f() AS rf ON true

sql: SELECT * FROM s.t NATURAL JOIN s.t2 ON s.t.id = s.t2.t_id

sql: SELECT t.id FROM s.t JOIN USING (id)

sql: SELECT t.id, t.name, t2.label, p.kind FROM s.t LEFT JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id JOIN s.parent AS p ON t.id = p.id WHERE t.id IS NOT NULL
note: mixed LEFT JOIN and INNER JOIN with WHERE

sql: SELECT t.id FROM s.t JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id AND t2.amount > 0

sql: SELECT COALESCE(a.id, b.id) AS id FROM s.t AS a FULL JOIN s.t AS b USING (id)
note: FULL JOIN USING with COALESCE on join column

sql: SELECT * FROM s.t JOIN s.t2 ON s.t.id = s.t2.t_id ORDER BY s.t.id
note: JOIN with schema-qualified column refs and ORDER BY

sql: SELECT count(*) FROM s.t JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id GROUP BY t.status HAVING count(*) > 0
note: JOIN combined with GROUP BY and HAVING

sql: SELECT t.id FROM s.t LEFT JOIN s.t2 ON t.id = t2.t_id WHERE t2.id IS NULL
note: LEFT JOIN with IS NULL filter to find non-matching rows
